THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT IN MFA No.201019/2019 C/W MFA No.201285/2021

The claimant in MVC No.1641/2013 has filed MFA No.201019/2019 seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the IV Additional District Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - XIII, NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 Vijayapura (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1641/2013 vide its Judgment and Award dated 28.10.2016.

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.201285/2021 is filed by the owner of the offending vehicle to modify the aforesaid judgment and award dated 28.10.2016 passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1641/2013 in so far as it relates to fastening liability on him to pay the compensation awarded.

3. The appellant in MFA No.201019/2019, who is respondent No.1 in MFA No.201285/2021 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'claimant' and the respondent No.1 in MFA No.201019/2019, who is the appellant in MFA No.201285/2021 shall henceforth be referred to as the 'owner' and respondent No.2 in both the appeals shall henceforth be referred to as the 'insurer' respectively of the LMV TATA ACE bearing registration No.MH-45/9610.

4 . The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 10.07.2013 at about 3.15 p.m. when he was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH- Latif S/O Mnik Attar vs Surekha And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78984093/
4 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 45/U-1646 (henceforth referred to as the 'motorcycle').

The claimant claimed that he and the rider of the motorcycle were proceeding towards Gherdi side and when they reached the land of Balaji Vithal Ligade within the limits of Kadlas village, their motorcycle was dashed against by a light goods vehicle - TATA ACE bearing registration No.MH-45/9610 (henceforth referred to as 'the offending vehicle').
As a result of the accident, the claimant suffered (i) fracture of the left S2 to S5 sacral alae (fracture of sacrum body) (ii) pubic symphysis diastasis and other injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the claimant was shifted to Disha Ortho Hospital,
Sangola, where he was treated as an inpatient for more than 15 days.

The claimant claimed that he was a coolie and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month and due to the accident, he was disabled and could not work as a coolie and therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') claiming NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 compensation of Rs.7,20,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

5. The owner of the offending vehicle contested the claim petition and alleged that there was contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and that he dashed against the offending vehicle after he lost control over the motorcycle.

He contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle and on the contrary, the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a valid licence to drive it as on the date of the accident.
The owner and insurer of the motorcycle were necessary parties to the claim petition.

The compensation claimed by the claimant was excessive and that the offending vehicle was insured with the insurer and the insurer is liable to pay the compensation that may be awarded by the Tribunal.
6. The insurer on the other hand, denied the accident as well as the negligence of the driver of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 offending vehicle.

It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a licence to drive a light goods vehicle and the accident occurred in Maharashtra State and the claimant and the owner were also from the same State.
It claimed that the vehicle did not carry a permit.
It claimed that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid driving licence to ride it and was negligent and caused the accident.
It claimed that the owner committed breach of the conditions of the policy of insurance and the insurer was not liable to indemnify the claim for compensation.
7. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.2.
He also examined a Doctor as PW.3, who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 22 to 25% to the left lower limb and spine and documents as per Exs.P1 to P16 were marked.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked documents as Exs.R1 to R4.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimant had suffered injuries in the road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It noticed the evidence of PW.3 and held that the claimant had suffered fracture of the left S2 to S5 sacral alae (fracture of sacram body) and diastasis of symphysis pubic.

In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal relied upon Ex.R4 - D.L. extract and held that the driver of the offending vehicle was licenced only to drive Light Motor Vehicle (Non-Transport) car with effect from 11.07.2012 as on the date of the accident and there was no endorsement in the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle authorizing him to drive light motor goods vehicle and therefore, the owner of the offending vehicle had violated the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance in allowing an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle.
Consequently, it fastened the liability to pay the compensation on the owner of the offending vehicle while exonerating the insurer of its liability to pay the compensation.

It directed the owner of the offending vehicle to pay compensation of Rs.89,800/- along with - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 interest at 9% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization.

He, therefore, submitted that the Trial Court must have pragmatically considered the disability - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 taking into account the evidence of PW.3.
He submitted that the Tribunal failed to award just compensation towards loss of income due to disability, loss of amenities and also failed to award just compensation towards pain and suffering.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the owner submitted that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited [(2017) 14 SCC 663], the driver of the offending vehicle was authorized to drive the offending vehicle and that the same did not result in violation of the conditions of the policy of insurance and the insurer could not escape the liability to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 13. Learned counsel for the insurer on the other hand submitted that PW.3 was not the Doctor who treated the claimant immediately after the accident and therefore, the evidence of PW.3 did not assist the Tribunal in any manner to assess the disability suffered by the claimant.
He, therefore, submitted that the Tribunal was right in awarding the compensation and there is no need to enhance the same.
14. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the owner and the learned counsel for the insurer.
15. The accident involving the two vehicles is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident for which he was treated.
The medico legal certificate at Ex.P10 discloses that the claimant had suffered fracture of the left S2-S5 sacral alae resulting in diastasis of the pubic symphysis.
It also discloses that there was pelvic compression and that the pelvic depression test turned out positive.
There was a restriction in the movement of the pelvic area.

The disability certificate (Ex.P15) issued by PW.3 corresponds with the medico legal certificate - Ex.P10 and therefore, the deposition of PW.3 that the claimant had suffered - 14 - Latif S/O Mnik Attar vs Surekha And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78984093/
7 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 disability at 22 to 25% to the left lower limb and spine cannot be ruled out merely on the ground that PW.3 was not the Doctor who treated the claimant immediately after the accident.

In that view of the matter, taking into account the fact that the claimant had suffered injury to the spine and the pelvic area, it is appropriate to consider the disability suffered by the claimant at 10% to the whole body.

Taking into account the fact that the claimant was aged 18 years as on the date of the accident and was a coolie doing hard labour, it is safe to consider his notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month and the disability suffered by him at 10% to the whole body.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is therefore not just and proper and the compensation to which the claimant in MVC No.1641/2013 is entitled to, deserves to be re-determined as follows:

In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the only ground on which the insurer attempted to avert liability is that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a licence only to drive a Light Motor Vehicle (Non-Transport) car and that he did not have an endorsement to drive a light goods vehicle.

This issue is no longer res integra in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), where the Hon'ble Apex Court was considering a similar case and it held as follows:
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 "60.1. "Light motor vehicle" as defined in Section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in Section 2(21)

A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a roadroller, "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d)
is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under Section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54 of 1994 and 28-3-2001 in the form.

60.3. The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act 54 of 1994 w.e.f. 14-11-1994 - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of Section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle"
in Section 10(2)(e), "medium passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(f), "heavy goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(h) with expression "transport vehicle" as substituted in Section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.

It does not exclude transport vehicle,
from the purview of Section 10(2)(d) and Section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

60.4. The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the owner of the offending vehicle contended that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a licence to drive a light motor vehicle (non-transport) car but there was no endorsement authorizing him to drive a light motor goods vehicle.
He contended that this issue is fully covered by the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan (supra).
He contends that both light motor vehicle and light goods vehicle were the same class of vehicles and therefore, the driver should be construed as authorized to drive both the vehicles.
Besides, he contended that the unladen weight of both the light motor vehicle and light goods vehicle did not exceed 7500 kgs.

The learned counsel for the insurer however contended that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a licence to drive a light motor vehicle (non- transport) car and not a light goods vehicles and hence, there was violation of the conditions of the policy of insurance.
34. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the owner and the learned counsel for the insurer.

35. In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the only ground on which the insurer attempted to avert liability is that the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a licence only to drive a light motor vehicle (non-transport) car and that he did not have an endorsement to drive a light goods vehicle.

This issue is no longer res integra in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited [(2017) 14 SCC - 27 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 663], where the Hon'ble Apex Court was considering a similar case and held as follows:
"60.1.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited [(2017) 14 SCC - 27 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 663]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Light motor vehicle" as defined in Section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in Section 2(21) read with Sections 2(15) and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act 54 of 1994.

60.2. A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a roadroller, "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d)
is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg or a motor car or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as Latif S/O Mnik Attar vs Surekha And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78984093/

sentences.text:
A licence issued under Section 10(2)(d)
- 28 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54 of 1994 and 28-3-2001 in the form.

The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act 54 of 1994 w.e.f. 14-11-1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of Section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle"
in Section 10(2)(e), "medium passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(f), "heavy goods vehicle" in Section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in Section 10(2)(h) with expression "transport vehicle" as substituted in Section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of Section 10(2)(d) and Section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

60.4. The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he - 29 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
The driver of the light motor vehicle is also eligible to drive a light goods vehicle and that would not result in any fundamental breach of the terms of the policy of insurance.
In that view of the matter, the appeal in MFA No.201314/2021 filed by the owner of the offending vehicle also deserves to be allowed.
36. Accordingly, the appeal in MFA No.201314/2021 filed by the owner of offending vehicle is allowed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As a result of the accident, the claimant suffered (i) fracture of the left S2 to S5 sacral alae (fracture of sacrum body) (ii) pubic symphysis diastasis and other injuries.
The claimant claimed that he was a coolie and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month and due to the accident, he was disabled and could not work as a coolie and therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') claiming NC: 2023:KHC-K:1348 compensation of Rs.7,20,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
He contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle and on the contrary, the driver of the offending vehicle possessed a valid licence to drive it as on the date of the accident.
It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a licence to drive a light goods vehicle and the accident occurred in Maharashtra State and the claimant and the owner were also from the same State.
In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal relied upon Ex.R4 - D.L. extract and held that the driver of the offending vehicle was licenced only to drive Light Motor Vehicle (Non-Transport) car with effect from 11.07.2012 as on the date of the accident and there was no endorsement in the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle authorizing him to drive light motor goods vehicle and therefore, the owner of the offending vehicle had violated the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance in allowing an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle.
The claimants claimed that the deceased was aged 25 years as on the date of the accident and he was serving in Spinning Mill,
Sangola and earning Rs.12,000/- per month and contributing to the family.
Hence, the claimants claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
26. The owner of the offending vehicle contested the claim petition and alleged that there was contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle / deceased and that he dashed against the offending vehicle after he lost control over the motorcycle.
In so far as the liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal relied upon Ex.R4 - D.L. extract and held that the driver of the offending vehicle was licenced only to drive Light Motor Vehicle (Non-Transport) car with effect from 11.07.2012 as on the date of the accident and there was no endorsement in the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle authorizing him to drive light motor goods vehicle and therefore, the owner of the offending vehicle had violated the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance in allowing an unauthorized person to drive the offending vehicle.
The Tribunal directed the owner of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation of Rs.12,47,000/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
